turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hey, yeah, nice to meet you too. Um, so I came in because I just... I feel like I’m literally crawling out of my skin whenever I’m supposed to sit still. Like, especially in the radiology suite at work, or in my classes. Actually, the chairs in my Tuesday lecture are those terrible plastic ones that are connected to the tiny desks? I don't know who designed those, but they're the worst. My buddy Josh tried to lean back in one last week and the whole thing just tipped over in the middle of a lecture. It was hilarious, the professor was so mad, he actually stopped the whole slideshow. But, uh, what was I saying? Right, so I've been trying to just tough it out for months now, just trying to sit normally, but I still just end up pacing around the control room, or shifting constantly, or finding literally any excuse to get up and move. I just can't stay put.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by an unrelated thought about a friend falling out of a chair and loses their train of thought, asking 'what was I saying?'.
symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient reports 'shifting constantly' when trying to sit still.
symptom_reasoning.S011: The patient reports finding any excuse to get up and move and pacing around in situations where they are expected to sit, like in class or at work.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient describes an intense internal feeling of restlessness, stating they feel like they are 'crawling out of my skin' when having to sit still.

turns.doctor_question: Did this feeling of needing to move start after you began a new medication or changed the dose of one?
turns.patient_response: Medication? Uh, no, I don't take anything. I mean, unless you count energy drinks? I had this phase a couple weeks ago where I was drinking those massive cans of Reign before my morning clinicals. The sour apple one is amazing, but it made my hands shake so bad when I was trying to position the X-ray tube. The lead tech, Brenda—she's been there for like thirty years—she actually snapped at me because I almost dropped a detector. Our backup portable machine is super old, it honestly looks like a literal washing machine on wheels. It’s so heavy to push down the hospital hallways, especially when the wheels get stuck on the elevator tracks. I always get the one with the bad wheel. But yeah, no, no prescription meds or dose changes or anything like that. I don't even take Tylenol most of the time.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a lengthy, rambling response with excessive unnecessary details to answer a simple yes/no question.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient's speech demonstrates tangentiality, wandering off-topic from medication to energy drinks, a coworker, and the wheels of an X-ray machine before returning to the original question.

turns.doctor_question: Since childhood, have you often had trouble paying attention or staying focused?
turns.patient_response: Trouble paying attention? Um, not really, no. I mean, I can focus just fine on stuff. Like when I was a kid, I could spend hours building those massive Lego sets. I had the Death Star one, the huge one with like four thousand pieces? My mom actually found it at a garage sale, which is insane because those things go for hundreds of dollars online now. The guy selling it was just trying to clear out his garage, he had all these vintage records too. Like original pressing Beatles albums and stuff. I don't really listen to vinyl myself, but my roommate Dave does. He brought this giant record player to our dorm and it takes up literally half his desk, so he’s always complaining he has nowhere to put his laptop when he studies. He had to buy this weird little lap desk thing off Amazon, but it's super flimsy. But, uh... wait, what were we talking about? Focus? Yeah, no, I don't think I've ever really had a problem with that.

symptom_reasoning.S002: The patient explicitly denies having trouble paying attention or staying focused, stating they can focus just fine.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by getting sidetracked by unrelated thoughts (Lego sets, garage sales, roommate) and forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, going on a long, rambling tangent in response to a simple question.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing voices when no one else is around?
turns.patient_response: Voices? Uh, no. Definitely not. I mean, the only thing I hear when it's quiet is just... regular stuff. Or like, the hum of the machines at the clinic. Seriously, the MRI machine is so loud, even from down the hall. It sounds like a broken washing machine mixed with a jackhammer. My buddy Josh actually tried to record it on his phone once to use as a sample for this music production class he's taking. He bought this massive synthesizer board last month with all these glowing buttons and sliders, it looks like a spaceship console. He spent like four hours on Sunday just hitting the exact same snare drum pad over and over while I was trying to study for my skull anatomy practical. It was driving me absolutely insane. I had to go sit in my car just to get away from the tapping. My car's AC is busted though, so it was like sitting in a literal sauna, and the cupholder is broken so I spilled my drink... but anyway, wait, voices? Yeah, no, no voices or anything like that.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being highly distracted by the extraneous noise of their friend tapping a drum pad while trying to study, to the point of having to relocate to their car.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient provides a highly verbose, rambling, and tangential response to a simple yes/no question, demonstrating excessive talking.
symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly and repeatedly denies hearing voices or experiencing auditory hallucinations.

turns.doctor_question: Have you had times when you felt unusually energized or up for several days in a row?
turns.patient_response: Energized for several days? Um, no, not like days in a row. I mean, I'm always kind of bouncing off the walls a little bit, but it's not like a multi-day high or anything. Like, yesterday in my radiation safety lecture, I literally couldn't stop tapping my foot, but that's just normal for me. That class is so ridiculously boring anyway. The instructor, Mr. Davis, he always wears these crazy bright ties, right? Yesterday's had these little cartoon hotdogs all over it. Like, who even buys a hotdog tie? Probably from one of those joke shops at the mall. I haven't been to the mall in forever, actually. The last time I went, I bought this phone case that the kiosk guy swore was completely indestructible, but I dropped it in the parking lot on the way to my car and the screen protector cracked immediately. The parking lot was being repaved too, so it smelled awful, like hot tar and chemicals, and my sneakers got this black sticky stuff on the soles that I still can't scrape off. I tried using a butter knife but it just bent the knife... but wait, sorry, what did you ask? Unusually up? Yeah, no, nothing like that. Just my regular energy.

symptom_reasoning.S010: The patient explicitly states they 'literally couldn't stop tapping my foot' during a lecture.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient describes their baseline state as 'always kind of bouncing off the walls a little bit.'
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting from a lecture to a teacher's tie, the mall, a phone case, and tar, before forgetting the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S033: The patient explicitly denies experiencing multi-day periods of feeling 'unusually up.'
symptom_reasoning.S034: The patient explicitly denies having multi-day periods of being unusually 'energized' or experiencing a 'multi-day high.'

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about everyday things?
turns.patient_response: Worrying? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't sit around stressing about stuff. Well, except maybe if I'm gonna be late, because I hate being late. But even then, it's not like a big worry. Like this morning, I thought I was gonna be late because my alarm didn't go off. Or maybe it did and I just swiped it off without waking up? I do that sometimes. I had to set my phone across the room for a while, but then I'd just get out of bed, turn it off, and get right back in. My bed is super comfortable though, I got this memory foam topper on sale at Target. Target is dangerous, honestly. You go in for toothpaste and you come out with a throw pillow, three bags of weird flavored chips, and a new lamp. I got these jalapeño popper chips last time that were so spicy I literally couldn't eat more than three. Dave ate the whole bag though, he has a stomach made of iron. We went to this questionable taco truck last week and he got the mystery meat burrito, and he was totally fine. I had a regular chicken taco and I swear my stomach was doing backflips all night. The truck was parked right next to the hospital too, which you'd think would make them more careful about food safety, but I guess not. They had this really cool neon sign though, it was a taco wearing sunglasses... wait, sorry, worrying? No, I don't really worry about everyday things much. Just normal stuff, I guess.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by a chain of unrelated thoughts (alarms, Target, chips, taco trucks) and temporarily loses track of the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, providing a long, rambling response that goes far beyond the scope of the doctor's question.
symptom_reasoning.S056: The patient explicitly denies worrying a lot about everyday things or stressing about stuff.
